title: Normalized lax tensor pairing for ringed direct image
statement: Let $(C,J),(D,K)$ be sites small relative to a fixed coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $v:C\to D$ induce direct image of sheaves by precomposition, let $R,S$ be commutative ring sheaves on $C,D$, and let $c:R\to v_*S$ be a unital ring-sheaf map. For $S$-module sheaves put $(PM)(U)=M(vU)$ with $R(U)$ acting through $c_U$, and let $P$ act on maps by precomposition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and regular modules as units, with their canonical associators and unitors [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. There is a unique lax monoidal structure on $P$ whose tensor map sends every local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ over $U$ to the local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ over $vU$. Here lax monoidal means natural maps $\mu_{M,N}:PM\otimes_RPN\to P(M\otimes_SN)$ and $e:R\to PS$ satisfying the associativity and both unit coherence identities. Its unit satisfies $e_U(r)=c_U(r)$ for every $U,r$.

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward) and 03EK (section-tensor-product, bilinear universal property); agent extraction of lax coherence and regular-unit uniqueness.

proof.text: The specified precomposition sends underlying sheaves to sheaves by hypothesis. For $r\in R(U)$ and $x\in M(vU)$ put $rx=c_U(r)x$. The ring-map equations give the module axioms, and for $a:V\to U$ naturality of $c$ gives $(c_U(r)x)|_{vV}=c_V(r|_V)(x|_{vV})$. Thus these are module sheaves and precomposition on linear maps is a functor, by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $e_U(r)=c_U(r)$. It commutes with restriction, is additive, and $e_U(ar)=c_U(a)c_U(r)=a e_U(r)$; hence $e:R\to PS$ is a module-sheaf morphism.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward: scalar restriction of direct image

proof.text: For $U\in C$ define $b_U:M(vU)\times N(vU)\to(M\otimes_SN)(vU)$ by taking the image of the sectionwise pure tensor $x\otimes y$ in the sheaf tensor. The construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] commutes with restrictions. It is additive in each input, and $b_U(c_U(r)x,y)=c_U(r)b_U(x,y)=b_U(x,c_U(r)y)$, so it is $R(U)$-bilinear for the three restricted scalar actions. The bijection of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], applied on $C$ with coefficient ring $R$ and target $P(M\otimes_SN)$, gives a unique module-sheaf map $\mu_{M,N}:PM\otimes_RPN\to P(M\otimes_SN)$ with this pure-tensor formula.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor and displayed bilinear universal property

proof.text: For $S$-linear morphisms $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, the two sides of the naturality equation $P(f\otimes g)\mu_{M,N}=\mu_{M',N'}(Pf\otimes Pg)$ send each local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ over $U$ to $f_{vU}(x)\otimes g_{vU}(y)$ in $(M'\otimes_SN')(vU)$. The tensor of maps has this formula from the sectionwise construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Injectivity of the bijection in [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] gives equality of these sheaf maps. This proves naturality in both variables.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: functoriality and bilinear universal property

proof.text: The canonical unitors of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] send $r\otimes x$ to $rx$ and $x\otimes r$ to $rx$. For the left-unit equation, the composite $R\otimes_RPM\xrightarrow{e\otimes1}PS\otimes_RPM\xrightarrow{\mu_{S,M}}P(S\otimes_SM)\xrightarrow{P\lambda_M}PM$ sends $r\otimes x$ to $c_U(r)x$, exactly the left unitor of $PM$. For the right-unit equation the composite $PM\otimes_RR\xrightarrow{1\otimes e}PM\otimes_RPS\xrightarrow{\mu_{M,S}}P(M\otimes_SS)\xrightarrow{P\rho_M}PM$ sends $x\otimes r$ to $c_U(r)x$, exactly its right unitor. In each case [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] promotes the equality on local pure tensors to equality of maps.

source.place: Tags 03EK and 03EO, section-tensor-product and lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor: canonical unitors

proof.text: Write $A=PM$, $B=PN$, $C'=PT$ and $H=P(M\otimes_S(N\otimes_ST))$. To test maps $(A\otimes_RB)\otimes_RC'\to H$, use the symmetry and tensor-Hom adjunction of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] to curry them to $A\otimes_RB\to\mathcal Hom_R(C',H)$. The bilinear bijection of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] tests these maps on $x,y$; by [def-pur-sheaf-hom], their values agree if their evaluations on every section $z$ over every further restriction agree. Thus it suffices to test the original maps on $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ over all objects. The associativity composite $P\alpha\,\mu_{M\otimes N,T}(\mu_{M,N}\otimes1)$ sends this tensor first to $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$, then to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ over $vU$. The other composite $\mu_{M,N\otimes T}(1\otimes\mu_{N,T})\alpha$ gives the same result. Here both associators are the canonical ones of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. The preceding test gives equality, the required lax associativity identity.

source.place: Tags 03EK, 03EO and 04TT: associativity formula, tensor-Hom adjunction and sectionwise internal Hom

proof.text: For any other lax structure $(\mu',e')$ with the prescribed pure-tensor formula, [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] gives $\mu'_{M,N}=\mu_{M,N}$ for every pair. Apply its left-unit identity at $M=S$ to $1_R\otimes1_S$ over any $U$. Using the canonical unitors [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], the left-hand composite has value $e'_U(1_R)1_S=e'_U(1_R)$, whereas the unitor has value $1_S$. Thus $e'_U(1_R)=1_S$. Since $e'$ is a morphism of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $e'_U(r)=r\,e'_U(1_R)=c_U(r)$ for every $r\in R(U)$. Hence $e'=e$, proving uniqueness of the whole structure and the asserted unit formula.
